title: Fifty become five
hook: fifty prayers are given, Musa urges him to ask for less, and five remain with the reward of fifty (Bukhari)
tomorrow: "If he said it, it is true"

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Mi'raj: welcomed at every heaven, as a son or as a brother. Your line was: met at every heaven.

Of everything that happened on the night of the ascent, what he carried home for his community to keep was a daily practice. And according to Sahih al-Bukhari, it started out much bigger than the one Muslims keep today, and it changed size because of a conversation with Musa on the way down. Today closes our week of sorrow and wonder: from Ta'if to the heavens, and back to the prayer mat. Fifty become five.
screen: `HE CARRIED HOME A PRACTICE.` → `IT STARTED BIGGER.` → `MUSA ON THE WAY DOWN.`

segments.voice: Bukhari keeps it in reports from Abu Dharr and from Malik ibn Sa'sa'a. At the highest point of the ascent, Allah enjoins on him and his community fifty prayers a day. He accepts and starts back down. He passes Musa, in the sixth heaven, and Musa asks: what were you commanded? Fifty prayers. And Musa, the prophet who led a whole people out of Egypt and through the wilderness, speaks from experience. In Bukhari's words, roughly: your community won't be able to bear it. I have dealt with people before you. Go back and ask your Lord to lighten it. So he goes back, and it is lightened. Down again past Musa, and Musa says the same thing: go back. Back and forth, the reports say, until it is five. And Musa says, still too much, go back once more. Here the Prophet says something very human: I have asked my Lord until I feel ashamed. I am content, and I accept. Then the word comes: they are five, and they are fifty. My word does not change. So the number got smaller, and the weight didn't. Look at who helped. Not an angel, but Musa, an older prophet who had led a difficult people and knew what daily life does to good intentions. And look at the week behind us: a man refused at Ta'if, comforted with grapes, offered revenge and refusing it, carried to Jerusalem, welcomed at every heaven. What he brings back down is five times a day.
screen: `FIFTY PRAYERS ARE GIVEN.` · `MUSA: YOUR PEOPLE CAN'T BEAR IT.` · `BACK AND FORTH, UNTIL FIVE.` · `THEY ARE FIVE, AND THEY ARE FIFTY.` · then, large: `FIVE, WEIGHING FIFTY.`

segments.voice: If you pray, picture where each of today's five prayers will fit, dawn, midday, afternoon, sunset and night, naming the place and the moment for each. If you don't, choose five moments to stop for one breath, morning, noon, afternoon, evening and before sleep, and see each one now, in order. Small, fixed, five.
Musa. In the sixth heaven he told the Prophet to ask again and again, until fifty prayers became five, with the weight of fifty still kept. Today's word.
Your line: five, weighing fifty. Small enough to keep, heavy enough to matter. A week complete, and day seven hundred fifty-six.

screen: `DAY 756 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: "IF HE SAID IT, IT IS TRUE".`

howItsDone: Muslims pray the five daily prayers, salah, at dawn, midday, afternoon, sunset and night, and the story of how fifty became five is taught with the Mi'raj.

chat.says: Is it true the daily prayers started out as fifty?
options: Yes; Musa sent him back until it was five, and the five still weigh as fifty.
No, they began at five, and Musa asked for them to be raised to fifty.
Yes, and Muslims who pray five still owe the other forty-five later.
chat.meaning: In Bukhari's reports Musa sent him back again and again until fifty became five; then the word came: they are five, and they are fifty.

Abu Dharr.meaning: a companion who narrated the report

Malik ibn Sa'sa'a.meaning: a companion who narrated the Mi'raj report

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 349 (Abu Dharr: fifty prayers enjoined; Musa urges him to go back; 'they are five and they are fifty; the word does not change with Me')
Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 (Malik ibn Sa'sa'a: Musa says he has dealt with people before; 'I have asked my Lord until I feel ashamed; I am content and I accept')

notes: The size of each reduction differs between reports; the script says only 'back and forth until five' to avoid a wrong count.
The reward-of-ten detail was left out under the claims rule; a Keeper may add it with a citation.
Bukhari 349 and 3207 numbers cited from memory; confirm which report holds 'until I feel ashamed' and 'I have dealt with people before you'.
'The prophet who led a whole people out of Egypt and through the wilderness' summarizes the Qur'anic Musa; confirm.
Day 756 is a week end; the hook and teach look back at days 750–755.
Practice: 'if you pray, aim to pray all five today' follows the outline; non-praying listeners get five breath stops.
The five prayer names in the practice (dawn, midday, afternoon, sunset, night) are given in English only; a Keeper may add Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha.
